h1: The 8 Best eGPU Enclosures and Docks for an RTX 3060, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: eGPU Enclosures for RTX 3060: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 eGPU enclosures and docks for an RTX 3060, scored on power options, controller, handheld PC support and card clearance.
summary: The ORARA 750W enclosure is the safest all-in-one home for an RTX 3060, with a supply that handles the card with room to spare. The ANQUORA ANQ-L336 is the best compact dock for handheld PCs, with confirmed ROG Ally X and MSI Claw 8 support, and the External eGPU Enclosure with a 240W supply is the portable choice for a short travel kit.
intro: An RTX 3060 is the friendliest card in eGPU land. It draws roughly 170 watts, fits in most cases, and does not need Thunderbolt 5 to be worthwhile. That frees you to choose on other grounds: how portable the box is, whether it can charge your laptop, and whether the maker has bothered to confirm compatibility with the handheld or ultrabook you actually own.

Eight boxes and docks are ranked here, from a full 750W enclosure to bare docks that accept your own power supply. Scoring covers power flexibility, controller, link speed, portability and compatibility notes. A 40Gbps Thunderbolt link will hold back a 3060 somewhat, but less than it holds back faster cards.

products.name: ORARA eGPU Enclosure Thunderbolt 3/4/USB4 40Gbps with 750W PSU
products.verdict: A 750W supply that leaves a 3060 hugely overpowered in headroom, with a JHL7440 controller.
products.description:
The ORARA ships with a 750W supply and a JHL7440 controller, supporting a 32Gbps daisy chain over Thunderbolt 3, 4 and USB4. Its card bay measures 13.7 inches long, 6.17 tall and 2.3 thick, so triple-slot designs are out.

For a 3060, the supply is more than enough, and nearly every 3060 is a two-slot card that fits the clearance. It wins because it is complete: no extra supply to source, no case to find. The 750W unit is overkill, so you are paying for headroom you will not use, which is the reason to look at smaller options if cost matters.

Buy it if you want a no-fuss box that will accept a bigger card later. Skip it if you want something small and cheap.
products.idealFor: A simple home eGPU that can grow.

products.name: ANQUORA ANQ-L336 Mini eGPU Enclosure, 40Gbps Thunderbolt 3/4 USB4
products.verdict: A mini dock with confirmed ROG Ally X and MSI Claw 8 support and flexible power options.
products.description:
The ANQUORA ANQ-L336 uses a JHL7440 controller delivering 32Gbps through PCIe 4.0 x4, with confirmed ROG Ally X and MSI Claw 8 support, and accepts ATX, SFX, FLEX or DC power.

Confirmed compatibility is rare in this category, and handheld gaming PCs are among the fussiest hosts. It ranks second because it needs a separately sourced power supply, so the total cost and build effort is higher than the ORARA's.

Buy it if you game on a handheld and want a proven pairing. Skip it if you want a finished box.
products.idealFor: Handheld PC gamers adding a desktop GPU.

products.name: External eGPU Enclosure with 240W PSU, Thunderbolt 4/3 & USB4
products.verdict: A 240W supply, a carrying case and dual Thunderbolt ports with 85W and 15W power delivery.
products.description:
This enclosure includes a 240W supply and a carrying case, supports GPUs up to 205 by 150 by 55mm, and has dual Thunderbolt ports with 85W and 15W power delivery.

A 240W supply is the right size for a 3060, which draws around 170W, leaving a modest margin. Because it includes a carrying case, it is the one that makes sense in a laptop bag. The 55mm height limit means a slim, two-slot card only. It ranks third because the margin leaves no room for a more powerful card later.

Buy it if you travel with your GPU. Skip it if you may upgrade to a power-hungry card.
products.skipIf: You plan to upgrade the card.

products.name: Maskedfish eGPU Enclosure Thunderbolt 3/4 USB4 40Gbps PD 85W Charging (MK-L18)
products.verdict: An open frame with PCIe 4.0 x16 mode and 85W charging that takes any card length.
products.description:
The MK-L18 uses JHL7540 or JHL7440 controllers in PCIe 4.0 x16 mode, has 85W PD charging and dual Thunderbolt ports, and its open frame has no GPU length limit.

It makes sense for a 3060 because the card is easy to power from a small supply, and an open frame stays cool without fans. It ranks fourth because it lists no included supply and gives a bare setup experience.

Buy it if you have a spare supply and like tinkering. Skip it if you want an enclosed unit.

products.name: VIKINYEE Thunderbolt 3/4 eGPU Enclosure USB4 (VK-Y900)
products.verdict: An ENIG-plated board with JHL7440/7450 controllers and dual Thunderbolt ports with 85W charging.
products.description:
The VK-Y900 uses JHL7440 or JHL7450 controllers on an ENIG-plated board, with dual Thunderbolt ports at 15W and 85W PD and support for newer RTX 50 and RX 9000 cards.

ENIG plating protects contacts from corrosion, which suggests care in the manufacture. For a 3060 it is a capable base. It ranks fifth because the listing omits supply and clearance details.

Buy it if you want a quality board for a DIY build. Skip it if you want a finished enclosure.
products.idealFor: DIY builders who value board quality.

products.name: Mini eGPU Enclosure Thunderbolt 3/4, USB4 40Gbps External GPU Dock
products.verdict: A JHL7440 mini dock with a pre-purchase compatibility check and SFX, ATX, FLEX and DC power support.
products.description:
This mini dock uses a JHL7440 controller, supports SFX, ATX, FLEX and DC power, and offers a detailed pre-purchase compatibility check.

The compatibility check saves returns, since eGPU problems usually come from laptop firmware, not the dock. It ranks sixth because it is a bare dock with no host list in our data.

Buy it if you want to confirm compatibility before ordering. Skip it if you need a complete kit.
products.idealFor: Cautious buyers who want to verify fit.

products.name: External GPU Dock Station, Mini eGPU Enclosure Thunderbolt 3/4 USB4 40Gbps
products.verdict: A JHL7440 dock that also acts as a USB-A and Thunderbolt 4 hub.
products.description:
This dock accepts ATX, SFX, FLEX or DC 12V power, uses a JHL7440 controller with a 32Gbps daisy chain, and also works as a USB-A and Thunderbolt 4 hub.

The hub function means one cable can serve both the graphics card and peripherals. It ranks seventh because it ships without a supply or case and gives no clearance data.

Buy it if you want a graphics dock that doubles as a hub. Skip it if you prefer a full kit.

products.name: PCIE 3.0 x16 22Gbps eGPU Dock with Thunderbolt 4 Cable
products.verdict: A JHL6340 dock at about 22Gbps with four power inputs and confirmed Legion Go compatibility.
products.description:
This dock uses a JHL6340 controller for roughly 22Gbps transfer and offers 4 power input options: CPU, Molex, PD and DC5521. It lists confirmed Legion Go compatibility and sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

The controller is older and slower than the JHL7440 docks, so a 3060 loses more performance. It earns a spot because it is the cheapest way in, and it names the Legion Go. It ranks last because 22Gbps is about half the link of the leaders.

Buy it if you want the lowest-cost entry for a Legion Go. Skip it if you want full bandwidth.
products.idealFor: Cheap entry on a Legion Go.

whatMatters.detail: An RTX 3060 draws about 170W, so a 240W supply is adequate and a 750W supply is plenty. Smaller supplies leave less margin for a later upgrade. Check the card's rated draw.
The JHL7440 gives about 32Gbps of usable bandwidth, while the older JHL6340 gives about 22Gbps. A faster controller lets a 3060 run closer to desktop speed.
Handheld PCs have quirky USB4 and Thunderbolt implementations. A dock that names your device, like the ANQUORA for the ROG Ally X, removes guesswork.
A kit includes a supply and case, so it works on arrival. A bare dock needs a supply you provide and some wiring care. Choose by your comfort with PC hardware.
A port with 85W power delivery can run a laptop and the GPU from one cable. Lower wattage only trickle charges.

faq.q: Is an RTX 3060 worth putting in an eGPU?
faq.a: Yes, particularly with a handheld or thin laptop that has weak graphics. It loses less to the 40Gbps link than faster cards do.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Assuming every Thunderbolt port works. Some handhelds and laptops are unreliable with eGPUs. Choose a dock that lists your device.

faq.q: Is the ORARA worth it over a bare dock?
faq.a: If you do not own a supply, yes, since it is complete. If you have a spare SFX unit, a dock is cheaper.

faq.q: Do I need a power supply for a bare dock?
faq.a: Yes. You supply an ATX, SFX, FLEX or DC unit and connect the card's power cables yourself.

faq.q: Will it work with a Mac?
faq.a: Apple silicon Macs do not support external GPUs for graphics. Intel Macs with Thunderbolt 3 may, with limits.

faq.q: How much performance do I lose?
faq.a: Some, because the link carries less than a desktop slot. The loss varies by game and by link speed.

finalTake: The ORARA 750W enclosure is the simplest, safest home for an RTX 3060, with a supply that handles the card with room for an upgrade. The ANQUORA ANQ-L336 is the best choice for handheld PCs, and the 240W kit is the travel option. Pick a dock that names your device and check the link speed.
